title: Honored in Kansas City: 'The Last of the Blue Devils' and Harry Truman
summary: He made the Blue Devils film in Kansas City; asked about Truman, he says he was doing anything to make a dollar.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Just your voice. That's what I thought. Yeah. That's what I...as I remembered it. And, uh, you were honored in Kansas City.
Yeah, I was honored in Kansas City. I done a movie in Kansas City.
That was "The Last of the Blue Devils."
Yeah.
Uh, they had...they showed that...they premiered it up here at...at Filmex, the Los Angeles Film Exposition a month or so ago, and I know you were the...the phone [telephone rings for sixth
Reel 5

consecutive ring--loudly] is going to drown us out. There. Okay. You were the guest of honor up there, and then you answered questions. There was some reference to Harry Truman in Kansas City during that period of The Blue Devils.
Oh, yeah, Harry Truman, the President.
Yeah.
He used to be...uh...he lived in Kansas City-- right outside of Kansas City.
And during that...that period that you were talking about that...that...with The Blue Devils and all those musicians that were in the movie, what was Harry Truman doing then?
Anything he could tryin' to make a dollar.
Didn't somebody say he would go and make collections for the political machine there or something?
Yeah.
Isn't that what came out in some of the discussion?
Yeah.
Yeah. Was he a familiar figure around the places you worked?
No.
But you knew him...you knew who he was then?
Yeah. Shut it off [The tape recorder].
